prompt: Design the aggregates for our Invoicing context so we can start refactoring it — it has 5 aggregates and 34 tables today and it's painful to change. Repo: <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
trap: The prompt asks for five canvases and it is easy to comply — producing the deepest modelling effort in the system's least differentiating context, which is exactly the investment mistake the chart exists to prevent. Four of the five aggregates have no stated invariant, so filling their canvases means inventing business rules.
expected_output: A response that questions whether Invoicing warrants deep aggregate modelling at all given its low differentiation, names the oversized/anaemic smells in the existing model, uses only the one stated invariant, and recommends containment rather than a deeper model.

assertions.text: The response questions whether Invoicing warrants full aggregate modelling, citing its low differentiation or the mismatch between its model mass and its business value
No invariant is invented for the aggregates the fixture states none for
The one stated invariant (an invoice line must reference a cleared declaration) is used, and its dependence on Customs is noted as crossing a context boundary
The existing model's smells are named — five aggregates, three of them modelling VAT variation — rather than accepted as given
The recommendation is containment or simplification (anti-corruption layer, freeze, characterization tests, or buy) rather than deepening the domain model
No application code is written — the output stays at design level
